headlines.title: Man rescued from inside garbage truck in San Francisco
headlines.description: A man was rescued from inside a garbage truck early Wednesday morning in San Francisco, according to the fire department. Firefighters were dispatched around 4:11 a.m. to the 100 block of Mason Street following a report of a person trapped inside a Recology garbage truck. According to SFFD, the truck’s driver had been flagged down and told that someone could be heard yelling from inside the garbage area of the truck. About 25 firefighters responded to the scene, and the rescue operation took roughly two hours, according to fire officials. The man was eventually rescued and was conscious, breathing and talking before being taken to a hospital, according to a San Francisco Fire Department spokesperson. The extent of his injuries was not immediately known. A firefighter also suffered a laceration to the hand during the rescue and was taken to a hospital for stitches, fire officials added. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.
headlines.source: Joel Soria and Ginger Conejero Saab

headlines.title: Proposed church purchase of historic Antioch theater sparks community concern
headlines.description: A historic East Bay venue that has hosted performances and community events for nearly a century could soon have a new owner, raising concerns among residents about the theater’s future. The El Campanil Theatre in Antioch’s Rivertown district is currently in escrow to be purchased by a local church, with the sale potentially closing as early as October. Community members gathered at the venue for a public meeting to discuss the impending transition and raise awareness about the sale. “I think we need to start mobilizing people to let them know this place is being sold,” one community member said during the meeting. “I don’t think everybody knows that.” The property fell into financial struggles during the COVID-19 pandemic and was sold to an out-of-state owner. It went back on the market nine months ago. Last month, Legendary Movement Church raised the down payment necessary to acquire the building. For residents and preservationists, the sale threatens the last remaining venue of its kind in the area. “This is the last remaining theatre in our city that’s being operated as a theatre,” said Sharon Sobel Idul, president of the El Campanil Theatre Preservation Foundation. Local residents expressed heartbreak over the potential loss of community programming and shared personal connections to the landmark. “There’s no other place to have music revues, plays, this is the last one left,” said Antioch resident Lisa Schmidt. “We grew up here…first dates here…we did recitals here,” added Antioch resident Michelle Fanucchi. Eli Herrera, lead pastor of Legendary Movement Church, attended the community meeting to hear residents’ concerns directly. He emphasized that the church aims to support the local area, though church services and events will take priority once the deal is complete. “This is the message I’ve given our church. We’re not a church in the city, we’re a church for the city,” Herrera said. Herrera noted that while the church wants to work with the community, external events will need to adapt to the new owner’s calendar. “Like any owner that takes over a building…when you go in its your house, we’re not fitting into the schedule they have because otherwise they would be purchasing the building,” Herrera said. The property remains in escrow, and the current owner hopes to finalize the sale by October.

headlines.title: Did we find dark matter? Here's how a Bay Area lab is helping with the possible breakthrough
headlines.description: Dark matter is legendary. It’s given credit for possibly explaining how the universe works, but we’ve never been able to actually identify it, until now – maybe. On Tuesday, excitement was high in the science community, especially in the Bay Area, due to a possible dark matter discovery. Among the researchers spending decades searching for dark matter are those working at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in Menlo Park. They say it’s early – after all, they’re looking for something that’s invisible – but if what they found truly is dark matter, it could open up a lot of new science.

headlines.title: Demolition company donates hundreds of items from razed Millbrae inn
headlines.description: A South Bay company that tore down the historic El Rancho Inn in Millbrae gave away hundreds of beds and other furnishings from inside the rooms to those in need. Buccaneer Demolition in San Jose was hired to tear down the Inn, which was built in 1948 and featured in the movie “The Right Stuff,” to make way for more than 350 new housing units. The company decided not to destroy the furniture inside but instead set it aside to give away. Buccaneer Demolition Vice President Jose Uribe said they donated roughly 487 items, including mattresses, microwaves, coffeemakers, chairs and more. “It’s important to us as an organization to do our best to limit the debris in the landfill and try to reuse items that still have life, that serve purpose,” Uribe said. “There’s a lot of value in a lot of the items that we salvage.” Most of the furnishings were donated to Farmworker Caravan, which supports agriculture workers from Gilroy to Half Moon Bay. Executive Director Darlene Tenes said for some clients the mattresses and bed frames were a game changer. “Sometimes when they get a bed, it’s the first bed they’ve ever slept in,” Tenes said. “They’ve never had a bed before. It’s such a huge, big gift.” Furnishings from some of the demolished rooms were also donated to Bay Area Furniture Bank, which supports the unhoused population, domestic violence victims and low-income families. Buccaneer Demolition also donated a statue from the inn to a Millbrae historical museum.

headlines.title: Colorado Fire: Wildfire near Yosemite burns 250 acres, prompts evacuations
headlines.description: Firefighters are responding to a wildfire burning near Yosemite National Park in Mariposa County. The Colorado Fire, which started Tuesday near Highway 140 and Colorado Road, has burned 250 acres in the Midpines area and remains at zero percent containment, according to Cal Fire. The cause of the blaze remains under investigation. As of Tuesday afternoon, the fire was moving at a moderate rate of spread toward the Merced River drainage. A total of 126 personnel from the Cal Fire Madera-Mariposa-Merced Unit are deployed to the incident, supported by 14 fire engines, four helicopters, three water tenders, two bulldozers, and three hand crews. Numerous air tankers from across the state are also making fire suppression runs as weather conditions allow. Crews are attempting to construct control lines to hold the flames north of Colorado Road, east of Telegraph Road, west of Buffalo Road, and south of the Merced River. Colorado Fire prompts evacuation orders in Mariposa County Emergency officials have issued mandatory evacuation orders and warnings for several zones in Mariposa County due to the immediate and potential threats to life and property: Evacuation Orders: Issued for zones Mariposa 546, 548, and 549. Residents in these areas are lawfully ordered to leave immediately. Evacuation Warnings: Issued for zone Mariposa 550 and 551. Those who require extra time to evacuate or have pets and livestock are advised to leave now. An evacuation shelter for residents and small animals has been established at New Life Christian Church, located at 5089 Cole Road in Mariposa. County officials have set up accommodation for large animals at multiple facilities and can be reached for arrangements at 209-967-3615. Road closures in effect due to Colorado Fire near Yosemite Road closures remain in effect, including state Route 140 from Briceburg to the Bug Hostel. Cal Fire reports that 45 structures are threatened by the fire, down slightly from earlier estimates. No injuries or destroyed structures have been reported. Yosemite still open while crews battle Colorado Fire Yosemite National Park remains open and is not currently threatened. “Crews will continue their fire fight throughout the night to control the fire and mitigate further damage,” Cal Fire said in a statement Tuesday night.

headlines.title: New video shows Eric Swalwell's stop by federal agents at SFO
headlines.description: Newly released surveillance video shows former East Bay Congressman Eric Swalwell being approached and escorted through San Francisco International Airport by federal agents. The footage was released by airport authorities in response to a public records request by NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit. The video appears to show federal agents approaching and surrounding Swalwell near the gate shortly after his arrival to San Francisco’s International Airport on Aug. 15. Swalwell, who is seen wearing a black hoodie sweater and baseball hat, appears to cooperate as he hands what looks like his cellphone to a female agent. He is seen carrying a backpack and rolling suitcase as the agents escort him through the airport, up an escalator and into a restricted area. Court records show federal agents executed a search warrant at SFO at approximately 8:25 p.m. The property inventory identifies the seized items as a white Apple iPhone, a charging cable and adapter, and an Apple MacBook Pro. The following day, federal agents searched Swalwell’s Washington, D.C., residence. He has not been charged with a crime. California Aug 20 Congress Apr 13 Publicly available warrant records cite a federal civil rights statute, Title 18, Section 242, which makes it a crime for someone acting under government authority to willfully deprive another person of federally protected rights. Multiple women have accused the former congressman of misconduct, including sexual assault and sending unsolicited explicit messages. Swalwell has denied the allegations, describing them through his attorney as false and politically motivated. Swalwell resigned from Congress and ended his campaign for California governor in April after the allegations became public. Before his resignation, the House Ethics Committee had announced its own investigation, while emphasizing that opening an inquiry did not mean a violation had occurred. The FBI previously declined to comment on the circumstances surrounding the airport encounter. Swalwell and his attorneys have not addressed the incident.

headlines.title: Sunnyvale launches city-run ride-share service with $3.50 rides
headlines.description: Sunnyvale is launching its own on-demand ride-share service, offering trips throughout the city for $3.50. The new service, called Sunnyvale Beam, operates similarly to Uber or Lyft but is run by the local government. The city contracted with Via Transportation to operate the service, which is partially funded by a state grant. “It’s really important for people to try the service. We think people are going to like it, and the first three rides are free, so people can try it risk-free,” a city representative said. Anyone in Sunnyvale can download the Beam app to request a ride. The service also offers rides to Homestead High School and Kaiser Medical Center in Santa Clara.

headlines.title: Apple's new CEO, John Ternus, takes over from Tim Cook after 15 years
headlines.description: Apple’s new CEO John Ternus takes the helm of the iconic tech giant on Tuesday, ending Tim Cook’s 15-year tenure during which the company’s value skyrocketed to $4.6 trillion thanks to the iPhone’s enormous popularity. The transition to a new CEO comes at a pivotal time for Apple. Artificial intelligence has unleashed the greatest upheaval within the industry since Steve Jobs unveiled the first iPhone in 2007. Apple has gotten off to a rough start in AI after stumbling in its efforts to deliver new features built on the technology, as promised nearly two years ago. Earlier this year, it unveiled new artificial intelligence advances, including upgrades to its Siri assistant, emphasizing a focus on privacy and day-to-day use as the iPhone maker tries to catch up with rivals. Ternus faces challenges that will force him to step outside his comfort zone in hardware engineering. Beyond finding ways to keep Apple competitive in the artificial intelligence race, he will need to navigate supply chain questions and relationships with figures such as President Donald Trump, who offered public praise for his predecessor on Tuesday. Serving as Apple CEO will also require soft skills, including developing relationships with important figures. Cook cultivated ties with Trump as he navigated the company through business challenges, including Trump’s trade and tariff war targeting countries in Asia, where Apple has extensive manufacturing supply chains. Although he is handing over the CEO reins at Apple, Cook is widely expected to help the company maintain a good relationship with Trump after he shifts to his new role as executive chairman. Ternus worked on some of Apple’s signature products under Cook, including the Apple Watch, AirPods and Apple Vision Pro. He will headline next week’s launch of the latest iPhone at Apple’s Cupertino, California, headquarters.
headlines.source: The Associated Press | The Associated Press

headlines.title: I-80 off-ramps to Treasure Island reopen after overturned vehicle
headlines.description: An overturned vehicle on Interstate 80 temporarily closed off-ramps to Treasure Island Road on Tuesday, according to the California Highway Patrol. The crash prompted the closure of the eastbound and westbound I-80 off-ramps to Treasure Island and Yerba Buena Island. The off-ramps reopened around 2:12 p.m. Motorists were advised to expect delays in the area. No information about possible injuries was immediately available. This is a developing story. headlines.title: Prolific South Bay burglar busted again on suspicion of burglary
headlines.description: A man who was convicted of dozens of burglaries in San Jose was arrested on suspicion of more of them, police said Monday. On Aug. 17 just before 5 a.m., officers responded to a report of vandalism of a business in the 3100 block of Senter Road. Investigators found that a man threw a brick through the front door of a business, “causing thousands worth in damages,” the department said. The suspect fled the scene before police arrived. Detectives identified Jonny Miles, 42, as the suspect in that case. Investigators later linked Miles to an attempted burglary on Aug. 18 on East Capitol Expressway, where a rock was again thrown at a door that was then kicked down. The suspect fled the scene. According to police, Miles was arrested in July, allegedly mid-burglary, on suspicion of three other burglaries. He was again arrested on Aug. 20 in San Jose on suspicion of burglary. Miles was charged with 15 commercial burglaries in Santa Clara County in 2020, for which he served about two years in jail, according to police. After being released in 2023, he was then charged with 23 more burglaries and went back to jail until May of this year. Miles was in custody as of Monday, being held on suspicion of burglary.

headlines.title: Monterey County Sheriff's Office names suspects in infant death investigation
headlines.description: The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office on Monday released the names of two suspects wanted in connection with the death of an infant girl who was found by the side of the road. In all, there are three suspects in the case — 36-year-old Ofelia Garcia Ortega, 38-year-old Sergio Galvez Perez and an unnamed 14-year-old girl, the sheriff’s office said. Garcia Ortega was arrested on suspicion of child endangerment and subsequently bailed out of Monterey County Jail. Galvez Perez is still at large and is wanted on suspicion of incest, lewd or lascivious acts with a child under 14, lewd acts with a minor, unlawful sexual intercourse and child concealment. The 14-year-old girl is wanted on suspicion of murder, sheriff’s office officials said in a news release Monday. “Child Endangerment Detectives have determined that Sergio Galvez Perez is currently concealing the 14-year-old juvenile and preventing law enforcement from locating her,” according to sheriff’s officials. The newborn girl, who investigators are calling “Baby Angelita,” was found on the side of the road at about 8:30 a.m. in the 100 block of Struve Road in a rural area of North Monterey County on Aug. 1. She was declared dead at the scene and a postmortem forensic exam allegedly found that she had signs of traumatic injury, according to the sheriff’s office. Anyone with information about this case is asked to contact Monterey County Sheriff’s Office Detective Sgt. Nicholas Kennedy at (831) 755-3773 or Detective Richard Geng at (831) 759-7279. Anyone who sees Galvez Perez should call 911, sheriff’s officials said.

headlines.title: SF proposal would expand protections for renters facing eviction
headlines.description: A new ordinance proposed in San Francisco would increase protections for renters facing eviction over unpaid rent. The proposal, introduced by Supervisor Jackie Fielder and co-sponsored by five other supervisors, is also backed by Mayor Daniel Lurie. Under the city’s existing rent ordinance, tenants can face eviction for any nonpayment of rent. The proposed ordinance would increase that threshold to at least one month of unpaid rent. Lurie said the proposal would provide much-needed stability as San Francisco continues to see increases in rents and the number of evictions. Oakland and Berkeley have implemented similar laws setting the threshold for eviction at one month of unpaid rent.
